key_insight: The paper establishes non-asymptotic total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers of O(h|ln h|) with exact drift and O(h|ln h| + 1/M) with Monte Carlo drift.
engineering_relevance: These bounds guide time-step and Monte Carlo sample-budget choices for finite-horizon sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal distributions without relying on long-time ergodicity.
method: Derive Kolmogorov equation regularization estimates using the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula.
Analyze total variation error through weak error estimates for non-smooth test functions.
Bound time-discretization and Monte Carlo drift-approximation errors.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments illustrate convergence as the time step h and Monte Carlo sample size M vary, alongside sampler effectiveness.
watch_item: The bounds require drift regularity assumptions; the improved 1/M dependence is measured in total variation, unlike the prior 1/√M result in L²-Wasserstein distance.
paper_title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
